title: Epochal slab quarantine and occupancy-decay predictor to reduce KV fragmentation
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Background:
Paged KV caches in high-concurrency workloads show persistent fragmentation: small live slices spread across slabs force frequent copy/evict cycles, driving decode stalls and elevated tail latency during prefill waves. Existing LRU-like evictions and immediate reallocation expose us to re-fragmentation and repeated prefilling costs for tenants with bursty access patterns.

Goal:
Reduce long-term fragmentation and decode stalls by combining a short-term quarantine for recently-freed slabs (so adjacent free regions can be observed and coalesced) with a predictive occupancy-decay model that prioritizes eviction and compaction decisions based on estimated reuse probability. Add kernel-affinity hints so micro-compaction runs on copy-optimized kernels and avoid interfering with hot decode waves.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Epochal slab quarantine: when a slab becomes free, mark it as 'quarantined' for a tunable epoch window (default 2s). Quarantined slabs are excluded from immediate allocation and standard eviction logic but remain eligible for opportunistic micro-compaction. The quarantine window lets nearby allocations reveal coalescing opportunities before we allocate back into the hole.

2) Occupancy-decay predictor: maintain a light-weight, time-decayed score per slab (or micro-slice) that estimates probability of reuse in the next epoch. Score combines recent access recency, tenant request pattern (burstiness metric), and decode-wave phase. Use exponential decay to keep overhead minimal. This score influences eviction ranking and compaction prioritization.

3) Opportunistic micro-compaction: when contiguous quarantined area crosses threshold (e.g., > 3 adjacent micro-slices), schedule a micro-compaction job that merges fragments into a single free range. Compaction is rate-limited and scheduled with kernel-affinity hints to run on copy-optimized kernels (minimize interference with decode kernel lanes).

4) Decode-wave smoothing and backpressure alignment: coordinate quarantine epoch boundaries with decode wave pacing to avoid simultaneous bursts of prefill and compaction. If scheduler detects a prefill surge, lower compaction aggressiveness and extend quarantine slightly.

5) Telemetry/controls: add new metrics and runtime knobs: quarantine_window_ms, compaction_batch_size, occupancy_decay_tau, compaction_kernel_hint, compaction_rate_limit. Expose per-tenant compaction budgets and a kill-switch for emergency.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Quarantine adds a small temporary tail of unallocated memory but reduces churn and copy overhead for hot tenants. We keep quarantine short to bound memory impact.
- Predictive model is intentionally simple (exponential decay + burstiness factor) to avoid compute overhead in hot code paths. If useful, the model can be extended to a lightweight on-CPU sketch.
- Micro-compaction is best-effort and rate-limited to avoid starving decoders. Kernel-affinity hints allow compaction to be steered to GPU lanes optimized for memory copies.

Benchmarks planned:
- Staging scenario A (multi-tenant bursty chat): measure p50/p95/p99 decode latency, bytes moved per second, KV hit ratio, and token cost before/after.
- Staging scenario B (steady long-context generation): measure eviction churn and average allocation latency.

Expected improvements (targets):
- Reduce per-tenant re-prefill token cost by >= 12% on bursty traces
- Decrease compaction-triggered decode stalls (p99) by >= 25% in staging traces
- Keep additional memory held in quarantine < 3% of active KV pool under typical loads
acceptance_criteria: New metrics for quarantine_count, micro_compactions/sec, occupancy_decay_tau exposed in Grafana
End-to-end A/B run shows >=12% reduction in re-prefill token cost on bursty customer trace
P99 decode latency reduced by >=25% in targeted staging scenario
Quarantine memory overhead measured and under 3% in 95th-percentile run
Feature gated via runtime flag and per-tenant budgets; kill-switch available
comments: 2026-02-26 — Initial spike: reproduced fragmentation pattern from customer trace (trace id: t-20260224-bursty). Observed repeated small frees followed by immediate reallocation within 10-50ms, causing repeated prefill work. — Miguel

2026-03-02 — Design review notes: PM requested explicit per-tenant budget to avoid noisy-neighbor compactions. Design doc added in Confluence (see link). Also agreed to conservative defaults for quarantine (2s) and compaction rate. — Aisha

2026-03-05 — Prototype implemented: quarantine mask + occupancy score in allocator (staging branch: feat/kv-quarantine). Micro-compaction scheduler added with simple contiguous-run detection. Local unit tests added. — Miguel

2026-03-07 — Staging perf run #1: reduced re-prefill token rate by 9% (below target). Observed that compaction jobs occasionally coincided with decoder tail spikes. Need to add kernel-affinity hint and prefill-surge detection. — Perf team

2026-03-09 — Kernel-affinity: added lightweight hint in compaction jobs to prefer copy-optimized kernel lanes; implemented backpressure alignment to defer compaction during prefill surges. Staging perf run #2 shows 15% re-prefill reduction and p99 decode latency improved by 22%. — Miguel

2026-03-11 — PR opened for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2543 (includes allocator changes, scheduler, metrics, and feature flag). Added integration test for quarantine expiry and compaction correctness. — Miguel

2026-03-12 — Code review feedback from Erin (runtime) and Kiran (SRE): request for stronger invariants around cross-tenant compaction and an emergency toggle in Console. Added tasks for per-tenant quotas and Console control. — Aisha

Next steps: finish per-tenant budget work (ENG-39201), finalize default knobs, run broader customer traces, and prepare rollout notes for runtime-1.20. Plan canary on dedicated pool with low-risk tenants.
